text:
marta: Heads-up: HF jinja chat_template -> Redwood conversion is dropping the SYSTEM block when jinja default is an empty block. Repro below.

ash: Can you paste the original template + the converted prompt? quick repro helps.

marta: Sure — original snippet:
```jinja
{% if system_prompt %}
- role: system
  content: "{{ system_prompt }}"
{% else %}
- role: system
  content: ""
{% endif %}
- role: user
  content: "{{ user_input }}"
```
Converted Redwood prompt became:
```text
[role=user]
content: "..."
```
System block vanished.

samir: Two quick guesses: (1) the conversion drops empty strings instead of preserving them; (2) tokenizer special tokens or braces are being consumed by the HF tokenizer so the jinja default becomes a tokenization artifact and converter treats it as falsy.

ben: Can you run tokenizer.encode on a literal "" and on the template with the empty system content? sometimes the tokenizer will split or merge markers.

marta: Ran this locally:
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("\n- role: system\n  content: \"\\\"\n")
[3950, 2, 4001]  # shows split tokens around the empty content marker
```
So the converter's heuristic ("empty -> drop") fired.

ash: Another pain: HF chat_template uses jinja braces. If conversion doesn't escape braces or preserve raw blocks, the template engine can evaluate differently. Also role mapping in config.json matters — if role_map maps 'system'->'assistant' you'll lose semantics.

samir: Workarounds:
- Ensure converter preserves empty strings (explicit sentinel).
- Add a step: replace `content: ""` with `content: "[__RW_EMPTY__]"` then post-process.
- Add tokenizer check that special tokens are registered and never split.

marta: Tried sentinel approach. After conversion I get:
```text
- role: system
  content: "[__RW_EMPTY__]"
- role: user
  content: "hey"
```
Then runtime strips sentinel and system block exists. Tests pass locally.

eval-bot: [evals] ChatBench run: conversion-with-sentinel + 8-bit-quant => quality regressions: F1 -2.5%, ppl +4.2%. Need to validate whether conversion change or quantization is main culprit.

ben: Good to separate variables. Run the eval matrix: (a) original HF template served through HF runtime; (b) converted prompt with FP model; (c) converted + 8-bit quant. Compare. If (b) already regressed, conversion is suspect.

ash: I'll add a unit test in the onboarding parser: assert that templates with empty jinja branches produce a preserved system message (string), not a dropped node. Also add a tokenization sanity check.

marta: I'll open a tiny issue + minimal repro and push the sentinel patch to the conversion tool. linking it here: https://github.com/redwood/inference/PRs/3456 (WIP)

samir: Also recommend adding explicit special_tokens in model config.json ("additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>"]) to avoid splits.

marta: Thanks all — will follow up with eval numbers. :thumbsup:
